name: Cure Natural Aqua Gel

card.summary: A Japanese water-based exfoliating gel that rolls dead skin and excess oil off the face, leaving smoother-looking skin.
card.note: Patch testing is advised by the maker for sensitive skin.

quick.overview:
Cure Natural Aqua Gel is a gel exfoliator from the Japanese brand Cure (Toyo Life Service). It is rubbed over the skin until small white beads of dead skin and oil form, which are rinsed away, giving a smoother, brighter-looking surface.

The brand says the formula is about 90 percent activated hydrogen water and is free of fragrance, colour and microbeads. It launched in Japan in 2003 and is marketed in many countries.
quick.how: Per the brand, a few pumps are massaged gently onto clean, dry skin for about a minute until beads form, then rinsed with lukewarm water. The Japanese maker states daily use is suitable, while US guidance suggests one to three times a week.
quick.risks: The maker advises a patch test for sensitive skin and avoiding eyes and mucous membranes. No independent clinical trial of the product was found.

lead: Cure Natural Aqua Gel is a gel-type exfoliating cleanser from the Japanese brand Cure, operated by Toyo Life Service. It is used to slough off dead skin cells, sebum and light makeup, giving smoother, clearer-looking skin.[1]

According to the brand, the gel is about 90 percent activated hydrogen water with plant extracts such as aloe and ginkgo, and contains no fragrance, colourants, parabens, sulfates or microbeads.[1] It was launched in Japan in 2003 and expanded internationally from 2008.[1] The brand markets it as Japan's top-selling exfoliator, a claim made by the company.[1]

chain: Dead cells and oil form beads and are rinsed off
angle.text: Users apply it as a gentle chemical-physical exfoliant to remove dead skin and excess oil for a smoother surface and better product absorption.

infobox: Cure / Toyo Life Service Co., Ltd.[1]

paras: The product is a clear, unscented gel that turns into small white beads on rubbing, with no abrasive grit.[1] Listed ingredients include hydrogen water, aloe, ginkgo, rosemary extract and glycerin.[1]

Toyo Life Service sold hydrogen water equipment before developing the gel around 2003.[1] The brand reports international distribution in over 20 countries and retail awards, such as Watsons HWB Awards.[1]
Brand guidance describes applying a few pumps to dry skin and massaging about a minute before rinsing; frequency guidance differs by market.[1]
No studies found. The company cites general work on hydrogen water's antioxidant properties rather than trials of this product.[1]
